questions.prompt: Adult salsa and bachata classes most often sell in which way?

options.text: Drop-ins and class packs
Annual contracts only
Season tuition by the month
Free classes paid by tips

questions.reveal: Adult and open-level classes usually sell as drop-ins and packs. Monthly season tuition is the youth studio model.

questions.prompt: Besides tuition, which fees does a kids' dance studio commonly charge?

options.text: Locker and towel fees each month
Registration, recital and costumes
Booking fees on every class signup
Late fees for arriving to class

questions.reveal: Annual registration, recital or performance fees, costume fees and recital tickets sit on top of tuition.

questions.prompt: An owner says, “We're mostly kids, but we run adult tap and salsa at night.” How do you think about this studio?

options.text: Adult studio; skip the kids' needs
Kids only; adults are a side note
A hybrid with two ways of buying
Competition studio; ask about teams

questions.reveal: Hybrid studios often bill kids by monthly tuition and adults by drop-ins or packs. Discover both.

questions.prompt: A one-night-a-week salsa owner with a day job asks what he really needs. What's your best approach?

options.text: Pitch every add-on so he has room to grow
Be honest about what fits his size
Tell him he is too small for Momence
Push video on demand as a new income

questions.reveal: In the SALSAtlanta demo the AE was candid about which add-ons gave value at his size. Each plan is custom-built, so fit beats loading it up.

questions.prompt: A kids' studio owner says, “We lose a chunk of families every year after the recital.” What do you ask?

options.text: How many classes run each week
Which card reader the desk uses
How she reaches them to re-enroll
Whether teachers take attendance

questions.reveal: Re-enrollment is the worry. Find out how she reaches families before next season, then show tags and segments.

questions.prompt: How do dance studios commonly fill the summer dip?

options.text: Camps, intensives and drop-ins
Closing June through August
Raising tuition for summer only
Moving every class online

questions.reveal: Camps, intensives and drop-in classes bring summer revenue, and fall discounts turn summer students into year-round ones.

questions.prompt: An owner mentions “the company” and “solos, duets and trios.” What is she talking about?

options.text: Her payroll and staff teams
Her competition team dances
Her adult beginner classes
Her summer camp age groups

questions.reveal: Company or comp team, plus solos, duets and trios, means competition. Expect team fees and choreography fees.

questions.prompt: In a kids' studio, who should your discovery questions about payment and messages focus on?

options.text: The dancers who take the classes
The teachers who run each class
The judges at each competition
The parents who pay and decide

questions.reveal: The child dances, but the parent pays, reads the messages and decides whether to re-enroll.

questions.prompt: A partner-dance student wants to book for herself and her partner, who has never been in. What do you show?

options.text: Her partner makes an account first
The desk books him through POS later
A second spot in the same checkout
A gift card she sends him to pay

questions.reveal: Extra spots are built into checkout. The partner gets a contact record and their own waiver email.

questions.prompt: A salsa owner runs cards for walk-ins on a separate device and logs them as cash. What do you show?

options.text: A newsletter to past walk-in clients
Roster walk-ins, POS and card reader
An intake form for each new walk-in
The waitlist setting for full classes

questions.reveal: Add the walk-in from the roster and take payment through point of sale, with an optional Stripe card reader.

questions.prompt: What happens to a student's answers to a studio's custom checkout questions?

options.text: They can tag the client on the roster
They're deleted after the class ends
Only Momence support can view them
They post to the community page

questions.reveal: Studios set their own questions (level, experience, injuries), and answers can tag the client for the teacher.

questions.prompt: A ballroom owner wants to approve every private lesson before it's booked, to match teachers. What do you show?

options.text: Turn off privates and take calls instead
A class with one spot for each private
A lead form that emails her each request
Request-only appointments staff confirm

questions.reveal: Appointments can be request-only. Clients see availability and request a time, and staff confirm it.

questions.prompt: What does a term or semester do in Momence?

options.text: Bills the client a fee per visit
Limits the class to members only
Repeats the class with no signups
Enrolls a client in every session

questions.reveal: A term or semester is a multi-week series. The client enrolls in, and pays for, all sessions at once.

questions.prompt: A mom wants to book her six-year-old, who has no email, into a class. What do you show?

options.text: She creates a second login for her child
The desk adds the child by hand later on
Book for a child, linked to her account
She books herself and brings the child

questions.reveal: At checkout a parent can book for a child. A child with no email gets one generated and linked to the parent's account.

questions.prompt: How can a kids' studio charge families for a semester in Momence?

options.text: Installments plus a registration fee
Only one full payment before it starts
Only weekly drop-ins for each session
Only by invoice sent outside Momence

questions.reveal: A semester can require an installment plan with a registration fee, or let families pay in full.

questions.prompt: A studio wants only Level 2 dancers aged 8 to 12 to book a class. What do you show?

options.text: A note in the class description only
A survey sent before each new season
A separate schedule page per level
Membership and age limits on the class

questions.reveal: A class can be limited to certain memberships, which studios use for levels, and to a minimum and maximum age.

questions.prompt: An owner says, “Our system was built for dance studios.” What's the best response?

options.text: Say dance software is out of date
Agree, then ask what's still manual
Offer a discount to switch this week
Drop it and ask about her marketing

questions.reveal: Acknowledge the strength first, then find the manual work. That's where Momence can be better.

questions.prompt: It's October, and an owner says, “I can't switch anything mid-season.” What do you do?

options.text: Ask when the season ends; book then
Tell her switching only takes a week
Agree and close out the lead today
Offer free months to switch right now

questions.reveal: Respect the season. Find the end date and book a dated next step in the planning window before registration.

questions.prompt: Which discovery question best uncovers manual work at a kids' studio?

options.text: How many mirrors are in the room?
Which styles do you teach most?
How long have you been dancing?
How do you bill recital and costumes?

questions.reveal: Fees around the season are often handled by hand. Ask how they bill them today.

questions.prompt: Early in a call, a salsa owner says check-in at the door is his biggest headache. What should the demo do?

options.text: Save check-in for the end of the demo
Start with the marketing suite first
Lead with the door: roster and payment
Ask him to send a list of features

questions.reveal: In the SALSAtlanta demo the door came 20 minutes in. Lead with the prospect's stated pain.
